tips.comment: Another Abbot heads to Yarmouth today after a solid third at the track last October. He’s been gelded since and now makes his handicap debut off a mark of 75. With Cieren Fallon booked and a good draw, he could be primed for a strong run if he’s progressed over the winter.

I really thought that my selection would have run slightly better on her season debut at Doncaster late last month, but it was after a 107-day break, so may have needed it. Had some useful looking form last year and if running to that level here should go close. Not sure of the ability of the 7lb claimer on board, but that allowance looks very handy, and it makes this the lowest mark yet. Added to that the application of first time head gear may well do the trick.

Not only is INVINCIBLE CROWN dropping down to easier company here, he's also well drawn and potentially able to get involved, even if the hot fav does prove too good. Still early days for new connections, but showed some promise in debut season and has generally offered a bit more each time he's run for the stable. Finished sixth at Donny on turf season debut, but wasn't far away and could get even closer now.

The model I run suggests each way on Style King is the value bet here. This result has largely been driven by Style King having the highest RPR of the 10-runner field. Decent draw in stall 2 for this 5f dash and can run the rail if he gets a good jump.
Few decent performances on all weather and has a win on turf, winning over this distance at Beverley in July last year.

Started strong at Brighton in April and followed up with a commendable 5th place out of 8 in a handicap at Ripon just 18 days ago. A solid choice at 20/1 for an each-way bet, especially with a skilled jockey and a yard in top form.

Holds every chance here and should go close, I'm not certain that the first time blinkers will make much of an improvement but if it does - he will win easily. There is plenty of natural improvement to come from this son of Expert Eye.

The model I run suggests Rhythmic Acclaim can win this one. Rhythmic Acclaim lines up with the second highest RPR of the field but doesn't seem to be penalized in the weights. Lowest official rating leaves him carrying the lowest weight of the field. A good 13 lbs difference to some of the runners. Previous course winner so likes this race course, and looks to add another one here.
This horse does stay 7F as it showed at Kempton in a class five. Hollie Doyle takes the ride, which is eye-catching, and it looks overpriced to me.

Race 2 at Yarmouth today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,411 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 6-year-old gelding Finbars Lad from the John & Sean Quinn yard. He will be ridden by Cieren Fallon. This son of Territories has been knocking on the door for his 3rd win, has run well fresh before, and is coming off a 6-month rest. With Fallon booked for the ride, it can only be a positive too, so a good chance is on the cards today.
In good form coming into this one, a potential down side is that his record here is not that good. I believe that his current form will allow that to change this afternoon.
Dunlop trained 4-year-old and December Southwell 7f winner, one of three, should return fit now, fresh for the 2025 campaign. Chance.
Won at Lingfield in December and had some good runs on all-weather. Going for a new yard and back on turf, just worth a little look.

How Lovely made a strong impression when winning on debut at Southwell and returns with plenty of upside. She’s giving weight away but has a solid profile and could be the one to beat if she’s trained on over the winter.

Good form from the three main players in this novice stakes. The selection is the only runner with turf form and the benefit of a recent run. Good yard/jockey. Runner-up in her last start but well clear of the 3rd and 4th who both had good ratings going into that maiden race. She also receives a nice pull at the weights in this maiden race.

Twice raced maiden who impressed in debut run when 4th of 10 at Bath last September but found things a bit more tricky last time out when only 11th of 14 at Ayr. Now going up in class makes life difficult, but I think a shorter distance will suit her better and is very appealing on current price.
Some very expensive maidens line up for this Fillies Stakes, including a couple of new ones, but none more so than Nandita, who cost a massive amount. Top Yard and good jockey today.

Stable in flying form, so taking a chance here with a positive jockey booking. Expect this to move early, so going early to get the bigger price. Can't see this not being the favorite by the time the smart money comes, and heard good things about this one.

Fairly limited data to go on here for the opener of this Yarmouth race. Awaken looks the best value pick. The model result has largely been driven by Awaken's trainer having a high RTF% and has a very favorable draw in stall 1 for the opener.
Looked good on debut, 2 poor runs followed. Handicap debut here and a significant jockey booking to match. Up in trip here, has a good chance.

Risen Again lines up in the 15:32 at Yarmouth tomorrow, the Sky Sports Racing 415 'Confined' Handicap??'a Class 5 contest over 1 mile 2 furlongs and 23 yards. Trained by Alice Haynes and ridden by Kieran O'Neill, this 4-year-old gelding carries a weight of 9st 11lb and is rated 65. His recent form includes a second-place finish at Lingfield over 1m2f on 24 March 2025, and a fifth-place finish at Nottingham over 1m2f on 12 April 2025. 
The expected good to firm ground at Yarmouth should suit him, given his previous performances. With his consistent form and experience over the distance, Risen Again presents a compelling each-way proposition in this field.

Showed a bit more on his handicap debut which came at this track over a mile. Stayed on well that day to suggest that this longer trip is going to be a plus. This is a slightly better race but he is a pound lower and has a smart 5lb claimer to help his burden.

The model I run suggests Incan Empire each way is the value bet here. Incan Empire line up with the second highest RPR of the field but a very middle order weight to carry. Plenty of placed efforts but needs to go one better to get over the line first. Last ran 32 days ago so does have race fitness and a reasonable draw in stall 5
Still a maiden after 27 starts, but was placed here over this trip 13 days ago. Just maybe this 5-year-old colt could come good today in an ordinary-looking race. Small each way bet.

The model I run suggests Oh So Audacious should win this race. All of the horses in this race line up with a very tightly bunched RPR, but the official rankings mean a more distributed weight being carried in the 10-runner field. Oh So Audacious has a lower official ranking and therefore goes out carrying a lower amount. Previous distance winner and can match the others for the highest top speed on the card. Decent draw in stall 2 and last run 39 days ago, so should have race fitness.

Shaws Phoenix is lightly raced and is awaiting her maiden win. She has however put up decent displays on the first run of the season and may cause a surprise here. The trainer/jockey combo of Haynes and O'Neill are in good form at the moment so at these prices we're getting a bargain.

Race 6 at Yarmouth today is a Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,612 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Union Island from the Charlie Johnston yard, and will be ridden by Callum Shepherd. This son of US Navy Flag is a consistent sort and has been threatening his 4th win. He is distance-suited and warrants respect in this field.

Light Up Our Stars lines up in the 16:42 at Yarmouth tomorrow, the Eastern Power Systems Handicap??'a Class 6 contest over 1 mile and 3 yards for four-year-olds and upwards. Trained by Scott Dixon and ridden by apprentice Taryn Langley, this 9-year-old gelding carries a weight of 8st 13lb and is rated 52. His recent form includes a third-place finish at Brighton over 1m2f on 30 April 2025, and another third at Beverley over 1m100y on 24 April 2025. These consistent performances suggest he's in good heart and capable of holding his own against strong opposition. 
The expected good to firm ground at Yarmouth should suit him, given his previous successes on similar surfaces. With his proven ability over the distance and under these conditions, Light Up Our Stars presents a compelling each-way proposition in this field.

She was a beaten favorite last time out where she finished ahead of Garden of Eden, who has subsequently gone on to win a Listed race. This longer trip should suit, and Aiden O'Brien obviously has faith in her.
Nicely bred filly who won both starts, the last one a Listed race over 1 mile at Newmarket last November. Should improve as a 3-year-old and the stable is in top form.

Three career runs for the 3yo filly, form 441 and hopefully more progress this year after a winter break. Excuses on her last start - heavy ground. Plenty to like about her second start, in Group 2 company, only beaten 2L and the 1st and 3rd from that race finished 1st and 2nd in the recent 1000 Guineas. She should be a big player in this Group 3 contest.

Did nothing wrong on debut at Newbury when running down the leader in the final furlong and lengthening away impressively. Obviously stepping up today, but trainer Andrew Balding might have had this as the target as he won it last year.

The only win last season for See The Fire came here at York over nine furlongs in a Group 3 race but her other six runs were all at Group 1 level and she failed by only a neck when 2nd to Opera Singer in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood. She was a beaten favourite first time out at Sandown in a Group 3 when only 5th of 7 but only beaten two lengths and that should have brought her on.

The 4yo filly spent last year running to a decent level overseas in good races. Decent UK run on her return at the start of this month when 3rd in a Group 2 race, up against Group 1 capable runners. Can improve for the run in this Group 2 contest. William Buick in the saddle and no problem with the quick ground.
Looks sure to run a big race. He looks the EW steal, but I just feel See The Fire is a bit better. She is regally bred.

Hard to know if the handicap mark of 90 for Romieu is generous or not but this ex-French Godolphin gelding was very impressive making all on the straight mile at Redcar and is ideally drawn in stall 2 if he wants to go with the pace on the round mile at York.

Colts by Too Darn Hot tend to be right out of the top drawer and this unexposed one could be another. He was up against a future Group placed horse when 2nd on debut and has won his 2 starts since. He'll strip fitter after winning on the Aw last time out on seasonal debut and a return to turf is a positive since his easy win on decent ground at Goodwood has produced a stack of future winners. Stall 3 should be a positive and he fits the profile of many previous winners of this race.
Lightly raced and looks the type to improve this season in handicaps, especially with Moore booked. The easy novice win at Kempton looked decent, and the second has run well since in a handicap.

Best Rate, from the in-form Richard Hannon yard, is an intriguing contender. The stable has made a strong start to the turf season, with 10 winners in the last 14 days at a 16% strike rate. Still lightly raced, Best Rate has run five times, winning a Wolverhampton Novice over Christmas, earning a handicap mark of 83. Since then, he has shown promise at Kempton and on his turf debut at Newmarket, where he was positioned on the far side in a race that saw the winner come from last to first. Despite that, he shaped well over a mile. Now dropping back to seven furlongs, in what's likely to be a strongly run race, he remains unexposed on fast turf. Sean Levey is booked to ride, a significant choice given other options. If he gets a clear path, Best Rate could be a strong late challenger at a double-figure price.

A very consistent runner, especially on AW, but more recently on turf. Has run into a place or the top spot every race this year and is used to the winners enclosure. I suggest a place, but if Red Sand can be overcome, a win is a strong possibility.
Showed some decent progress this year with two places on the all-weather tracks and a win the last time out. Bit of an ask to keep going here, but a good each-way option.

Lightly raced 3yo filly. Two runs this year. Excuses last time out when not firing on her AW debut. Only beaten 2L on her return during March, in a very strong looking Listed contest against older runners. She wasn’t beaten far at this track last summer, on fast ground, in a Group 2 contest. She now drops into a class 3 handicap, her mark of 94 looks very handy and she’s now helped by a capable apprentice who is taking a useful 7lb off her back.

The model I run suggests the value play here is an each way bet on Tattie Bogle. Four places up for grabs on some platforms offer additional placings. The result of the model has largely been driven by Tattie Bogle having the highest RPR of the field and the second lowest official ranking. This leaves him carrying the second lowest weight for this 7f trip. He has shown some promise, finishing second in a class 4 handicap only four days ago, so clearly has race fitness. There are question marks around whether the turnaround is too quick. Drawn in stall 5, which is a bonus. On these shorter 5-7f trips, lower stall draws are statistically advantageous.

Won debut run at Hamilton last May and also gained valuable experience at this course when 3 of 8 last October. Had been off 7 months prior to LTO effort where rustiness was evident when only 9 of 12 at Newmarket earlier this month. Going down in class which should help.

Was finally rewarded by a big win after a series of promising runs when she landed the win at Pontefract last month. This is only her 2nd handicap run, and the mark has dropped by 3 lbs, but she still needs to improve as she is going up 2 classes.

The 4yo progressed nicely last year, winning 2 of his last 3 runs in 2024. He was a good 3rd of 13 on his return last month after a 7 month break - high RPR rating posted - and can take another step forward. He was a nice 4L winner on fast ground last year.
Unexposed and beat a fancied rival LTO at Redcar on handicap debut over 10f. Just 4 lbs higher here, and if staying the extra distance, must have a big chance as right end of weights.

Great Bedwyn is a horse who has outrun his odds both times he has run at York, which is a track that doesn't suit a lot of horses. He also seems to go well first time out and his trainer Richard Hannon is operating at a very good strike rate considering the number of runners he has.

The model I run suggests each way on Masekela is the best way to play this. Lines up with the joint highest RPR of the field and goes out carrying the lowest weight for this 1m 3f trip. Longer distance should make the weight differential more prominent. Last ran 10 days ago, so has race fitness and draw 7 isn't amazing but matters less over this distance.

Ey Up Its The Boss is a stalwart of the northern racing circuit and has put up some decent displays here. This is the first time he is upped to 12 furlongs and this may bring about some improvement. Good to Firm is his best surface and has won previously on his 3rd run of the season. His OR is currently 79 which gives him a great chance.
Has the advantage of being the only C&D winner in this field and in good form (3211). Not surprised the mark remains unchanged as he has bags of ability, so should be a contender.

Trainer Richard Fahey is respected at local York racecourse. Glistening Nights looked progressive last season. Four wins last year, all at ten furlongs, as handicap mark rose. Not the only one of these to try a new trip. Damsire is Sea the Stars so some chance the 4yo will stay. Clearly has a bit of ability (four wins from sixteen turf outings) and decent handicap chance - carries 9 stone. Oisin Orr (SR 15%) rides.
Can't resist a long shot in the last race. First run in nearly a year, but had a good spell last year, including a win here at York in July.

American Affair won very easily on reappearance, and has only gone up 4 pounds for that. I'm expecting the pace to collapse here, as there is so much pace. This horse will be in the perfect position to take advantage of this. I'm not sure if stall 16 is good here, but it looks like there's pace everywhere.

Shagraan has to shoulder top weight here, but he was really progressive as a 3-year-old last season, winning twice and placing (including extra places) a further four times in competitive handicaps. That saw his mark rise to 101, which was the same as his reappearance third when just 0.5L back on seasonal return and just 3lbs higher than when fifth here at the Ebor meeting on his only visit to York. He was the only one of the top six to race off the pace that day, meaning it can be massively upgraded. There's so much pace on offer here that there's the potential for a real burn-up, and his likely hold-up tactics can bear fruit. Now a 4-year-old, I think he can show himself to be a pattern performer at sprinting trips.

The 4yo was a winner of a 28-runner handicap at Royal Ascot last year on fast ground. Big Return ran three weeks ago, after a 6-month break, beaten under a length in a decent handicap - posting a big RPR rating. Room for improvement after that run.

The best form of Toca Madera has been on good to firm and firm going and he should be suited by conditions at York and should be in the first five home with Tommie Jakes taking off five pounds allowance.

Mondammej knows this track very well but has surprisingly never won a race here. He's a horse which comes off the pace, which is the profile I'm looking for here. He's down to a mark of 80 and showed promise on the All-Weather. Place shout at these odds.

The model I run suggests Frio is the most probable winner here for this race. This result has been driven by the fact Frio has the highest RPR in the lineup and all horses go out carrying the same weight. Good placing at Musselburgh a month ago, looks to build on that here. Nice low draw stall for a 5f dash is important.

The selection is making his debut in this average looking 6 runner novice stakes. The trainer has good career stats with his 2yo runners, sending out plenty of quality youngsters in recent years. You would expect he’d be using one of his better types with a first prize of £20K in this contest.

Courageous Strike will be a short price, but this two-time flat winner was very impressive in winning his second start over hurdles at Chepstow last month. He has his favored good ground again and should be able to follow up.

The model I run suggests Linden Lane can win this one. Courageous Strike is the huge odds-on favorite and doesn't represent value at 1.2s. Linden Lane has shown some promise in recent outings and placed in decent company. Should be the pick of the rest should something unexpected happen to Courageous Strike.

The model suggests Bardenstown Lad should win this one. Short-priced favorite, so more a question of value here. The model result has largely been driven by Bardenstown Lad having the highest RPR of the 6-runner field by some amount. Only carries 8 extra lbs for the trouble and has Edwards Vaughan on board, relieving a further 5 lbs.
Has more to offer over this trip after winning LTO after wind surgery. 5 lbs higher but has the scope for more improvement.

Double Dragon won at Ffos Lass last May, 2m good, and has run on softer ground on all three starts since. Not disgraced in any of them, and last run in January when 5th of 11 has seen the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 6th that day all win since. Back on good ground today with yard in top form, he does not need to do much more to win here. First time tongue tie goes on, and that could get a bit more from him.

The model I run suggests Getalead can win this one. This result has largely been driven by Getalead having the highest RPR of the field but doesnt carry much weight extra for the privelage. Significant pricing differences on some of the platforms for this horse show a difference of opinion in the market. 7s on B365 vs. 12s on WH.
Overpriced for a race of this nature. Doesn't have too much to do. Just lurking in the wings of leaders, pick them off 3 out, come 2nd near the last, assert on the run in. Easy task.

Won on penultimate start with 2nd franking form by winning next time. Then he was 2nd in follow-up bid, beaten by one who also won again next time. So, 2 good bits of form there. Ground suits. The one to be on.

The model I run suggests Time To Bite can win this one. Very open initial market for this 5 runner race shows it's largely down to behavioral pricing adjustments rather than the bookmakers having a firm view on who will win. The model result has largely been driven by Time To Bite having quite a bit less weight to carry than the other runners over this 2m 4f trip. He is also a previous course and distance winner recently, which adds some comfort. Won a class 4 race in Warwick 9 days ago, so comes here in good form.
Interesting field with five runners and no clear standout. Two wins in the last three, and has done well at this course before with a win and a third place.

The model I run suggests Robin Blue Breast could win this one. Robin Blue Breast steps out with the highest RPR of the field, and all runners here go out carrying the same weight. Takeonedayatatime is the current very short-priced market favorite, but that does not represent value here. Next best looks like Robin Blue Breast. Callum Pritchard is a trusted jockey on board and relieves a further 5 lbs off the total weight, which does give a competitive advantage over the 2m trip.

FALSE FLAG runs for a powerful NH yard and this filly may have found a suitable opening for her career debut. Her dam was a Bumper winner and there is the stamina in her family to think she is the right type to land a race of this nature.

Poor bumper race and worth a poke going each way with Musique Des Champs. Ran in a low-grade conditions race, finishing fourth. Now goes under rules for Kailey Woolacott, who does okay with her bumper runners. Still a filly, and she's by Jukebox Jury. The sire does well on good ground.
Beaten into second place last time out but could go better here. Decent record at Newton Abbot with a win and two places from three starts.

Unspeakable is a strong contender for this one at Newton Abbot. He won well at Taunton last time out. He quickened up well when asked. Now carrying 10st 4lbs for this race and Jack Tudor riding again he could well go in again.

Comes into this with plenty to prove at present, but has seen his mark drop from 117 down to 110, with the jockey taking off a further 5 lbs this time. 
He's 4 from 5 over CD, very much a track that suits him well. He started off his winning spree off a mark of just 74 and ended the winning run off a mark of 112, winning a better race than this one cosily. 
He placed behind a handicap blot off a 7 lbs higher mark than this nto, finishing a clear 2nd behind Wincanton course specialist Lord Accord. No disgrace there. 
Admittedly, he's not shown much since. Personally, I think his mark was just too steep. Now he's eased in the weights and in a weaker race, with a decent 5 lbs claiming jockey in the saddle. I think he can go well with conditions very much in his favour.

If anyone happened to watch this on his handicap bow here last time out, it is fair to say that he was tenderly handled. Probably didn't want to lose his novice status for the season ahead. Very interesting that Conor comes down to ride and I'm sure he is better than his current mark.
Disappointing last time out at Taunton on his chasing debut. Had been consistent over hurdles prior to that, the form of his last effort being boosted several times since by the winner.

Square Du Roy finished best of all in his latest run, which followed wind surgery, 271 days off, and a change of ownership. The way he finished in a competitive race saw him as a different horse to all previous starts, and runs like that will see him win races. 5lb out of the handicap here, but connections will know much more about him today and know when to pounce.

The model I run suggests each way on Kintaro is the value option here. 11 runner race with 3 places up for grabs. Kintaro lines up with the highest RPR of the field, but the lowest official ranking. This leaves him running off a very workable mark and goes out carrying the lowest weight of the field over this slightly longer 2m 2f round trip.
Ran well on handicap debut over a mile last time out, finishing 2nd to Zappata, who has won 3 times since. Just 1lb higher here and up to 10f should be a banker.

Ottoman is a lot more interesting than the form book on paper is suggesting returned to action on the 7th of April 2025 after a 161 day break having exchanged hands and joined a new stable in the process of that break now after 2 runs for his new yard he arrives here in a much fitter state and is better adjusted back home at his new yard steps up in trip going over 1 mile 2 furlongs for the first time that being a good move by his connections as this new trip can unlock a whole new level of improvement currently operating on a very dangerous mark of 54 O Greenall & J Guerriero's new recruit looks poised to trouble the judge on this outing jockey Aiden Brookes takes off a handy 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims here in what is a suitable assignment for this individual likely to be a whole different proposition this time out especially over this new trip gelded son of Acclamation & Kaftan ( Dam's sire Dansili ) must be taken very seriously of this sort of mark and shouldn't be by any means underestimated
Not a lot appealing here, and I like a flyer each way with four places to show. Hasn't shown a lot on all-weather but is coming off probably the best run so far, finishing fifth at Wolverhampton.

This horse is friendless at 50/1 in the early market and comes with the proviso that she'd only really be of interest if there was any market support since this is a gambling stable. Reasons for thinking we might see a marked improvement, though, are the first-time cheekpieces and the first-time booking of Jason Watson on the horse. His strength in the saddle looks exactly what is required since the horse hasn't been straightforward for weaker jockeys. The step up in trip will also suit and help the horse settle, and progeny of the sire do really well on firm ground, which often occurs at Bath and doesn't suit many horses. In fact, the sire's progeny have a record over c&d on firm ground of 11353020, which is 2 wins and 3 places from just 8 runs, which suggests the 50/1 might be worth taking.

Baileys Value lines up in the 20:12 at Bath tomorrow, the Blackmore Building and Design Handicap??'a Class 6 contest over 1 mile 2 furlongs and 37 yards. Trained by Lemos Souza, this 3-year-old filly by Bated Breath has shown gradual improvement in her recent outings. 
After a series of unplaced efforts, she stepped up to 1m1f at Wolverhampton in March, finishing a respectable third at 66/1. Her latest run at Brighton over 1m2f saw her finish sixth of nine, suggesting she's finding her stride over these longer distances. 
Returning to turf on Bath's firm ground could play to her strengths. With George Wood taking the ride, Baileys Value presents a compelling each-way proposition in this field.

A touch disappointing on his return to action this season, hammered off the boards at Windsor but was only able to plug on at one pace for third. This stiffer finish could be a help to him and he is entitled to sharpen up for the run.
Goes for the HT reverting to turf. Both wins were on AW, but Dam won on quick ground, as did his sire. His full brother was rated in the 80s at his peak, so should be able to win off 62.

At the bottom of the handicap mark in this field, but at least gained valuable experience over C&D last September. Now makes handicap debut tomorrow, and if improvements are made, then I think he has a chance, which is helped by dropping down in class.

Jimmy Mark thrives at Bath, with three career wins at the course and a recent victory over this trip. He’s well-suited to firm ground and front-running tactics, making him dangerous if allowed to dictate. The Kittow-Hornby pairing adds further confidence. A genuine contender with conditions in his favor.

Blue Hero returns to a track he likes and runs off a mark close to his last winning one. He was a solid third over course and distance last time out and should be competitive again if fit and ready after a break.
Unseated over hurdles last time. Possibly didn't stay on penultimate start when going for the HT. Worth an each-way bet back down in trip.

Endofastorm lines up in the 19:42 at Bath tomorrow, the Best Odds Guaranteed At Yeeehaaa.Bet Handicap??'a Class 6 contest over 1 mile 3½ furlongs for three-year-olds. Trained by Joe Ponting, this 6-year-old mare by Galileo Gold has shown a consistent profile, with 3 wins and 4 placings from 27 career starts. 
Her recent form includes a third-place finish at Wolverhampton on 6 May 2025 in a Class 5 handicap over 1m5f219y, where she was beaten by just over 11 lengths. Prior to that, she secured a victory at Wolverhampton on 9 December 2024 in a Class 6 race over 1m4f51y on the all-weather surface. 
The expected firm ground at Bath should suit her, given her previous successes on similar surfaces. With her proven ability over the distance and under these conditions, Endofastorm presents a compelling each-way proposition in this field.
Has had a pretty good time of it in 2025, on turf and all-weather, with a win here at Bath last time out and has placed five times in seven starts.
Travelled strongly over 6 furlongs at Wolverhampton and kept on when 4th of 12 and beat 2 lengths last month. Of interest with this slight in drop in trip and uphill finish on turf debut.

Race 1 at Bath today is a Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,152 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 6-year-old gelding Sisters In The Sky from the G Harris yard, and will be ridden by Tyler Heard. This son of Showcasing is a 7-time winner with two of those over this course and distance. He has been a consistent performer in recent times, and signs are that his 8th win is on the cards. Must be considered today.

Midnight Flame is still searching for his first win after 33 attempts, and the handicapper has given him a good chance to break his duck here. He disappointed last time out, but that was over the minimum distance, and this extra furlong will play much more to his strengths.

If you look back at the Yarmouth form over 6 furlongs earlier in her career, that form has taken a massive boost, and she hasn't run on that surface since. Blinkers go back on and could be primed for a big run for a trainer that goes well at the track.
Ran a race stacked full of promise first time out at Leicester and sure to come on for that. Extra half a furlong here will suit and sure to be hard to beat.

Race 2 at Bath today is a Maiden (Class 4) for 2-year-olds over 1,152 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2-year-old gelding Eightthreeone from the Eve Johnson Houghton yard, and will be ridden by Georgia Dobie. This son of Rumble Inthejungle had a decent debut at this course when a good 2nd earlier this month. He should improve on that showing and is one to consider.
A winner when last seen at this venue. She was strong at the finish that day, suggesting this longer trip is well within range. She has a 5lb penalty, but that looks fair. She has a big chance.

Happy Index won over 2m4f here in September and again at Market Rasen in November. He returned from a break when 3rd here over 3 miles last month. He should appreciate the step up to 3m2f on quicker ground, and with Sean Bowen booked to ride, he looks the most likely winner here.

Assuming Schmilsson can jump the larger obstacles he can win this very ordinary Novice Handicap Chase. His hurdle form is well in advance of these, and the top weight is one who I can always readily avoid as he isn't the most resolute of animals.
Still on a very workable handicap mark despite a slight nudge in the weights. Very consistent, will relish this trip at this venue, and you can never write off Lucinda Russell horses in Scotland.
Green Sky should take this race by the scruff of the neck and win. He had Let's Mingle behind when second to Roxanne (winner since), and JJ Slevin has one ride today at Perth.
Could be a race to second with a strong favorite in this race, but could challenge here too. Second at Catterick the first time over hurdles.
More than a year since his last win, but his mark has been steadily dropping and has now reached a level where he can be competitive, carrying only 1 lb more than on his last victory.
Hasn't done much lately but had a good spell last year with back-to-back wins, including one here at Perth, and not much else standing out.
Somptueux has won two of his three points this spring, likes a sound surface, and has Gina Andrews on board. So his long trip north to Perth should be a winning one.
First run for a new yard but has been remarkably consistent at Perth before without a win. Finished in the top four in all five starts, placing three times here.

This race looks pretty desperate and I am convinced that Wotsmyname could finally shed his maiden tag. He's travelled a lot sweeter since being fitted with cheekpieces and I believe the eight-year-old has every chance off a 9lb lower mark than his latest fourth at Kelso, where he only gave way on the run-in.
Ran best run to date and was a little unlucky, having met trouble in running when making progress after 2 out. Finished with running left and is worth backing here.

The yard seemed to have found the key to Larkfield Lusive last time. He joined just over a year ago and, following racing over various trips and ground, went as close as he's been a month ago. Still only 6 years old, and connections will get more from him yet. This race looks like a winning opportunity.

MILLYUPDAHILLY drops considerably in class following a fair effort in a much deeper handicap latest. She is race-sharp with potential to be seen to much better effect in this company , and not yet fully exposed under this code in Britain with this trainer having recorded multiple wins at this venue she should be heavily involved.
Back from a break having last run in mid December. Vastly experienced, has won four times here at Perth, and conditions could be good here.

PRINCE NINO is back to a workable mark and has previous course form so maybe he reverses the slide in form before too long. Lighter in the weights than when placing here last September and could get involved if the return here helps. Claimer takes further weight off and he's dangerous to rule out too readily.

Sunny South West won on rules debut in a bumper at Clonmel in March and then ran well to finish 5th in a Grade 1 at Punchestown when 66/1. This is much calmer waters, and if he runs to the same level, he should be winning here.
Won well at Galway last time out and is in with a real chance here as long as overcoming the nine and a half months' break.
Won his bumper on debut on penultimate start before being overfaced in a Listed race last time. Back down in grade here, has every chance.

ANGELO DUNDEE is often well punted and some of his placed form in Bumpers reads even better than his career debut win. He has a promising 7lb claiming cionditional jockey aboard and he rares the value play with his fitness worth chancing.
I can't look beyond the market leader in this race as Patty O'Farrell, who has been steadily improving recently and should improve further from a good 2nd place last time out.

GIMME A BUZZ given time represents a high-profile yard and surely has something to spare from his lowly handicap mark. He is ridden by Mark Walsh on behalf of J P McManus and this is a weak handicap where he should be capable of landing a blow.

As always, I’m looking for a bigger price, and one that interests me is Fran Flood’s 7-year-old mare SPANISH MAID. This charge posted some solid efforts in maiden hurdle company, most notably a 3rd (beaten 2 lengths) here at Tipperary last May. That was followed by a 3rd & 4th at Sligo and 5th at Fairyhouse. This daughter of WORKFORCE was then sent over fences, taking on the likes of Zenta, Paggane, and Springt De La Mare - all of whom have progressed nicely since.
The return to hurdles looks the right move. Despite her bloodline, her best run came here at Tipperary on yielding ground. Nearly all of her other runs (bar one) were on testing ground, so it’s interesting to see how she fares today on the current good/ yielding surface. Donagh Meyler retains the ride and has a respectable 20.97% place strike rate at Tipperary over the past five years. Trainer Fran Flood hasn’t had a winner since 2022, but a return to the scene of his mares best performance offers some hope. At current odds of 25/1 with 5 places on offer, I wouldn’t be putting the mortgage on her. but hitting the frame certainly isn’t impossible.

Slowly improving over hurdles and was a close up 4th at Leopardstown two starts ago running a lot better than odds of 100/1 might have suggested. Was let down by his jumping next time at Navan and had made several mistakes before coming to grief late on. Bounced back to form at Limerick last time when a close 3rd over 21f. Further improvement cannot be ruled out and hard to leave out of calculations and holds solid claims.

Bitofajokelike almost landed as a 125/1 shot when runner-up at Cork last time out over this distance. It's easy to see why the market respect is emphatic here in a serious drop in field quality after that impressive showing.

Backward type who has had only 3 runs under rules, despite being 5 years old. Won his bumper last November despite being green, and greenness let him down in follow-up bid in December. Made hurdles debut last time out 6 weeks ago and is likely to improve from that.

Related to a couple of reasonable sorts, winners over hurdles, a chance is taken on Jonathan Sweeney trained Leading Light at a big price. One of just two newcomers in this maiden hurdle over 3m1f. By Gold Cup and St Leger winner Leading Light, pedigree suggests this lengthy trip will suit.

This modest chaser remains winless after 18 hurdle races. However, she achieved a commendable 5th place out of 12 in a handicap hurdle at Clonmel 3 months ago. Now facing a longer distance. The stables potential is uncertain, but the jockey brings a valuable 7lb claim. At odds of 66/1, this could be a smart each-way wager if the duo clicks.

Navy Waves has only won 1 of his 23 starts, and that was at Thurles back in November 22. He has, however, been placed in 3 of his last 4 starts. He was 2nd of 16 at Thurles in March and then third twice at Limerick and Clonmel last month. He is off the same mark but steps up from 2m1f at Clonmel to 3m1f here. He was 3rd at Kilbeggan over this distance last July, so looks like a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.

SPATMAN DE CERISY with his sound NH sire runs for a shrewd Irish yard who would not have too many handicap hurdlers rated as low as 90. This lightly-raced six year old has likely had this race as his off-season target given he was placed here last year and often well found in the market his chance looks at least as strong as others.

Brian McMahon’s 6-year-old French mare BARRYROE MADAM will need one to come out to get in from the 1st reserve spot, but should that happen, I wouldn't dismiss this daughter of KAPGARDE too quickly. Her last run also her best to date came 41 days ago at Naas (24f, Good/Yielding), where she threw down a serious challenge from off the pace to dispute the lead before falling at the last. The 1st and 2nd from that race have since run well off marks of 86 and 100. Ricky Doyle, in flying form with a 60% place strike rate the past fortnight, remains in the plate - a definite plus.
Clare-based trainer Brian McMahon may not be a household name, but his small yard boasts a solid 26.32% place strike rate at Tipperary over the past five years. This French charge was sent off at 14/1 last time and is currently trading around 16/1 off the same mark. Some might question the switch from undulating Naas to the flat, sharp Tipperary, but she’s also placed at Galway -a similarly sharp track. If she puts in a clear round, I wouldn’t be surprised to see her bang there at the finish.

PEBBLE TO A PEARL would have recieved a higher opening handicap mark had she finished closer to a couple of much higher rated types in her most recent qualifying run. She appeared to be capable of better and may well find her way over this trip in this sphere.

BOLD BROOK is clear top-rated as a later-starting low-mileage type still likely with plenty more to offer through the handicap sphere. His qualifying efforts suggest he is well treated dropped 2lb from his handicap debut and given time since his last start he could be the answer.
